correctness.rationale: On the flat lateral product cylinder, wrapped angular displacement is U~Uniform[0,1], axial difference V has density 2(1-v), independently; D^2/A=(qU^2+q^{-1}V^2)/2. In log q, every positive integrand is strictly log-convex for p>0, and the averaged moment diverges at both ends, ensuring a unique optimum. Symmetrizing the positive derivative at q=1 shows the optimum lies in (0,1). Direct integration gives q2=1/sqrt2, q4=3^(-1/4), and the exact minimum moments. Laplace endpoint concentration with uniform exponential domination yields q_p=1-2/p+o(1/p), with no claim of small-p monotonicity. Independent 140-node Gauss-Legendre quadrature reproduced q2, q4 and q100=0.9805634068287064, and the p100 scaled deficit near 2. Numerical work only checks instances, not the all-p argument.
